evidence: M-O s.v. yard: backyard (front and back reversed)
terms.comment: The counterpart of Traupman’s ārea postīca for the back yard (p. 409). antīcus “in front” is classical: Varro, antīca (pars) ad merīdiem, postīca ad septentriōnem (LL 7.7, Lewis & Short).

evidence: M-O s.v. yard: backyard (front and back reversed)
terms.comment: For a front garden that is planted rather than an open yard.

mo-yard.html: Morgan–Owens has front and back the wrong way round: it gives ārea anterior (v. antīca) and hortus anterior (v. antīcus) under “backyard” and ārea posterior (v. postīca) under “frontyard”.

sources: Lewis & Short: anticus · Lewis & Short: area
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. yard: backyard, yard: frontyard. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 409.
